warning: Every private key in this file is published test material and protects nothing. The key bytes are ASCII and read "postern v1 TEST VECTOR ...". Loading one of these keys into a running agent, operator client or hub would hand the door to anyone who has read this file.
notes: Offsets are zero-based byte positions inside the record named. Multi-byte integers are unsigned big-endian.
signing_input_hex is the exact byte string handed to Ed25519: domain_tag_hex followed by signed_region_hex.

The SPA request and the pong do not transmit their tag, so signing_input_hex is longer than the record's signed region. The bundle and the beat carry theirs at offset 0, so their tag is already inside signed_region_hex.
Every rejection vector is signed correctly over the bytes it carries, unless the vector is about the signature, so the field named in its description is the only reason to refuse it.

expect_trial_open of "accept" marks a record the wire layer admits: an action payload is canonicalised only once service_id has been resolved, which needs the host's configuration, so those vectors name the payload accessor that refuses them instead.

host.name: vector-host
host.role: opens SPA requests and bundles, signs pongs and beats

untrusted_operator.name: vector-untrusted
untrusted_operator.role: trusted by nothing in these vectors

domain_tags.note: Prepended to the 120-byte signed region for signing only. The datagram stays 224 bytes.
Prepended to the 58-byte signed region for signing only. The pong stays 122 bytes.
The record's first field. It separates the signature and lets a parser reject a record of the wrong type first.
The record's first field, for the same two jobs as the bundle's.

spa_rejections.name: datagram-shorter-than-the-record
spa_rejections.description: A 223-byte datagram, one short of the 224-byte record. The bounded-length check runs before any key is touched.

spa_rejections.name: datagram-longer-than-max
spa_rejections.description: A 1401-byte datagram, one past MaxDatagram. Padding up to MaxDatagram is accepted; beyond it the datagram is rejected on length so a padded packet can never fragment.

spa_rejections.name: reserved-byte-at-offset-3
spa_rejections.description: The reserved byte at offset 3 of the inner record is 1.

spa_rejections.name: reserved-byte-at-offset-118
spa_rejections.description: The first of the two reserved bytes at offsets 118 and 119 is 1.

spa_rejections.name: reserved-byte-at-offset-119
spa_rejections.description: The second of the two reserved bytes at offsets 118 and 119 is 1.

spa_rejections.name: unknown-version
spa_rejections.description: version is 2. v1 has exactly one legal value and there is no negotiation.

spa_rejections.name: unknown-alg
spa_rejections.description: alg is 2. Only 1, ed25519+x25519, exists in v1.

spa_rejections.name: unknown-kind
spa_rejections.description: kind is 3, which is neither gate nor action.

spa_rejections.name: action-with-non-zero-counter
spa_rejections.description: An action carrying counter 1. An action has no counter path, and a free counter would raise the operator's high-water mark.

spa_rejections.name: action-with-non-zero-ttl
spa_rejections.description: An action carrying ttl_seconds 1. An action requests no lease.

spa_rejections.name: gate-observed-payload-not-zero
spa_rejections.description: An observed-source gate whose payload byte 1 is 1. Every byte after source_kind is reserved.

spa_rejections.name: gate-asserted-unmasked-prefix
spa_rejections.description: An asserted 198.51.100.7/24: host bits survive below prefix_bits. A decoder rejects rather than masking.

spa_rejections.name: gate-asserted-v4-padding-not-zero
spa_rejections.description: A v4 assertion with a non-zero byte at payload offset 7, inside the 7..18 padding the 16-byte address slot leaves.

spa_rejections.name: gate-asserted-prefix-bits-above-family-max
spa_rejections.description: family 4 with prefix_bits 33.

spa_rejections.name: gate-asserted-unknown-family
spa_rejections.description: family 5, which is neither 4 nor 6.

spa_rejections.name: gate-asserted-reserved-tail-not-zero
spa_rejections.description: An asserted gate whose reserved payload byte 19 is 1. Bytes 19..31 are reserved for both families.

spa_rejections.name: confirm-reserved-tail-not-zero
spa_rejections.description: A confirm whose reserved payload byte 24 is 1. The wire layer admits it: which action variant applies depends on service_id, so the reserved tail is checked when the payload is read as a confirm.

spa_rejections.name: disarm-payload-not-zero
spa_rejections.description: A disarm whose payload byte 31 is 1. The whole 32-byte payload is reserved for a disarm.

spa_rejections.name: liveness-reserved-tail-not-zero
spa_rejections.description: A liveness ping whose reserved payload byte 16 is 1. Bytes 16..31 follow the challenge nonce and are reserved.

spa_rejections.name: key-id-disagrees-with-decrypting-operator
spa_rejections.description: A record naming the untrusted key's key_id, correctly signed by the trusted operator and sealed under the trusted operator's shared secret. Without this check anyone holding a trusted key could forge audit attribution.

spa_rejections.name: corrupted-signature
spa_rejections.description: A well-formed record whose signature has one bit flipped.

spa_rejections.name: sealed-by-an-untrusted-operator
spa_rejections.description: A well-formed, correctly signed record sealed from a key the agent does not trust. No precomputed shared secret opens it, which is indistinguishable from garbage and from a forgery by design.

pong.name: liveness-pong
pong.description: The one record postern transmits in reply, signed by the host key that also signs heartbeats and emitted only on the always-allow path after a liveness ping has fully authenticated.

pong_rejections.name: unknown-version
pong_rejections.description: version is 2. A receiver that reads a version it does not understand answers nothing.

pong_rejections.name: unknown-alg
pong_rejections.description: alg is 2. Only 1, ed25519+x25519, exists in v1.

pong_rejections.name: shorter-than-the-record
pong_rejections.description: 121 bytes, one short of the 122-byte pong record.

pong_rejections.name: longer-than-max
pong_rejections.description: 1401 bytes, one past MaxDatagram. Padding up to MaxDatagram is accepted and its trailing bytes discarded; beyond MaxDatagram the pong is rejected on length so a padded packet can never fragment.

pong_rejections.name: host-id-does-not-match-the-host-that-was-pinged
pong_rejections.description: A correctly signed pong naming a different host_id from the one the client pinged. The client compares in constant time against what it sent.

pong_rejections.name: request-id-does-not-match-the-ping
pong_rejections.description: A correctly signed pong echoing a different request_id. Echoing both request_id and the challenge nonce is what closes the replay hole; either alone would let a captured pong answer a later ping.

pong_rejections.name: challenge-nonce-does-not-match-the-ping
pong_rejections.description: A correctly signed pong echoing a different challenge nonce, the other half of the same pairing.

pong_rejections.name: timestamp-outside-the-freshness-window
pong_rejections.description: A correctly signed pong one millisecond beyond the client's freshness window, whose bound the vector publishes as verify_now_ms and verify_window_ms.

pong_rejections.name: corrupted-signature
pong_rejections.description: Every field matches the ping and one bit of the signature is flipped.

bundle.name: bundle
bundle.description: One policy bundle, signed by a bundle signer and then sealed anonymously to the host's encryption key. The seal authenticates nobody, so the signature carries the whole authenticity claim.

fields.policy_utf8:
version: 7
services:
  - name: ssh
    kind: gate
    proto: tcp
    ports: [22]

bundle.ephemeral_key_source: sha256("postern v1 TEST VECTOR bundle ephemeral bundle")

bundle_rejections.name: wrong-magic
bundle_rejections.description: The first byte of the 15-byte magic is not 'p'.

bundle_rejections.name: policy-len-disagrees-with-record-length
bundle_rejections.description: policy_len is one byte longer than the policy actually present, so the record length and the prefix disagree. Exact, not at least: trailing bytes would give one meaning two encodings.

bundle_rejections.name: policy-len-above-the-cap
bundle_rejections.description: policy_len is 0x00200000, twice the 1 MiB cap. The bound is checked before the prefix sizes anything, so a small record can carry an absurd prefix and still be refused cheaply.

bundle_rejections.name: shorter-than-the-fixed-length
bundle_rejections.description: 163 bytes, one below the 164-byte minimum a record with an empty policy occupies.

bundle_rejections.name: untrusted-signer
bundle_rejections.description: A structurally perfect record, correctly signed, naming a signer key outside the trusted set. Membership is checked before the signature, so an untrusted party's signature is never verified.

bundle_rejections.name: corrupted-signature
bundle_rejections.description: A trusted signer's record with one bit flipped in the signature.

beat.name: beat
beat.description: One signed heartbeat. It is not encrypted: it carries telemetry rather than secrets, and the hub checks it against the one signing key already on file for the host named inside.

beat_rejections.name: wrong-magic
beat_rejections.description: The first byte of the 13-byte magic is not 'p'.

beat_rejections.name: body-len-disagrees-with-record-length
beat_rejections.description: body_len is one byte longer than the body actually present.

beat_rejections.name: body-len-above-the-cap
beat_rejections.description: body_len is 0x00020000, twice the 64 KiB cap, in a record of a few hundred bytes.

beat_rejections.name: shorter-than-the-fixed-length
beat_rejections.description: 137 bytes, one below the 138-byte minimum a record with an empty body occupies.

beat_rejections.name: signed-by-another-key
beat_rejections.description: A structurally perfect record signed by a key that is not the one on file for this host. A beat carries no signer key field: the verifier is handed the one key the record must check against.

beat_rejections.name: corrupted-signature
beat_rejections.description: The host's own record with one bit flipped in the signature.

cross_protocol_rejections.name: spa-request-signed-over-the-untagged-region
cross_protocol_rejections.description: The signature covers the 120-byte signed region with no tag in front of it. The datagram decrypts, parses and matches key_id, so the signature check is the only control that can refuse it.
cross_protocol_rejections.signed_over: the SPA request's signed region, without postern-spa-request\0

cross_protocol_rejections.name: spa-request-signed-over-the-pong-signing-input
cross_protocol_rejections.description: A genuine operator signature over the pong's signing input, carried in an SPA request. The tags make the two sets of signable byte strings disjoint, so it cannot be reused here.
cross_protocol_rejections.signed_over: postern-spa-pong\0 followed by the pong's 58-byte signed region

cross_protocol_rejections.name: pong-signed-over-the-untagged-region
cross_protocol_rejections.description: The pong's half of the same check: a host signature over the 58-byte signed region with no tag in front of it. Every other field matches the ping, so the signature is the only control in play.
cross_protocol_rejections.signed_over: the pong's signed region, without postern-spa-pong\0

cross_protocol_rejections.name: pong-signed-over-the-spa-request-signing-input
cross_protocol_rejections.description: A genuine host signature over the SPA request's signing input, carried in a pong. Refused for the same reason as its mirror image above.
cross_protocol_rejections.signed_over: postern-spa-request\0 followed by an SPA request's 120-byte signed region
